page: Microsoft Azure D48lds_v6 is a compute-focused instance within the Dldsv6 family running on Microsoft Hyper-V. It is driven by a 24-core, 48-thread Intel Xeon 8573C processor with an x86_64 architecture and a maximum clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The CPU features a 260 MB L3 cache and supports specialized instruction sets, including AVX-512, AMX (amx_tile and amx_int8), VAES, and SHA-NI. The instance is configured with 96.0 GB of memory, resulting in a 1:2 core-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Local storage is directly bundled as a 2,832 GB NVMe SSD, while discrete GPU acceleration is not present.

Benchmark evaluations highlight strong computational and I/O capabilities. In synthetic processing suites, the instance achieves a Geekbench single-core score of 2,160.0 and a multi-core score of 20,188.0, alongside strong ratings in Clang software compilation (45,145.0) and ray tracing. Memory subsystems demonstrate high read bandwidth, reaching 3,685.22 GB/sec on cached small blocks and 255.6 GB/sec on uncached large blocks. In data-handling assessments, the system delivers 67.02 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and 81.17 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. CPU-based machine learning inference is also notable, generating 30.35 tokens per second on medium 7B models.

With its 1:2 vCPU-to-memory allocation, the D48lds_v6 targets environments where processing power and local disk performance take precedence over large in-memory capacities. This resource profile prevents over-provisioning memory for compute-heavy applications. The 2,832 GB local NVMe array provides low-latency temporary storage, though persistent workloads require supplemental network block storage. Given these characteristics, the instance is appropriate for software build servers, multi-threaded data compression, high-traffic web applications, database staging, and CPU-driven batch inference.
description: Microsoft Azure D48lds_v6 is a compute-aligned virtual machine configuration from the Dldsv6 family, delivering 48 dedicated vCPUs backed by 24 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running up to 4.2 GHz. Equipped with 96 GB of system RAM, it maintains a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio optimized for compute-intensive workloads that require less memory per thread than standard configurations. The instance includes 2,832 GB of fast local NVMe SSD storage and incorporates 260 MB of L3 cache, along with Intel AMX and AVX-512 instruction extensions. Benchmark results demonstrate strong throughput in multi-threaded decompression, software compilation, static web serving, and database transactions, alongside robust local memory read and write bandwidth. The absence of a discrete GPU makes it less suited for heavy model training, but CPU-based inference remains viable. Microsoft Azure D48lds_v6 is well matched for Clang build pipelines, Redis caching clusters, high-frequency web serving, and large-scale data transformation.
